summary: I sent the prompt from the script, and the agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development. It asked one worktree question, which I answered with "use whatever the skill recommends". It then ran all six tasks in one turn: for each task it dispatched an implementer subagent and then a reviewer subagent. It ran the 240s short soak itself in the foreground. It started the 720s long soak in the background, dispatched the final whole-branch review, and then held its turn open with a blocking wait until the soak finished. After that it offered merge/PR/keep. I answered "merge back to main locally", and it fast-forwarded main to d5efa36. I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: All four criteria pass, and each is backed by session-log tool calls, git history on the main checkout, and matching checksums for the soak tests. The agent's turn stayed alive through both slow soak commands, and it never stopped mid-plan except for the opening worktree question.

observations.description: Startup showed a 'Newer Opus model available — Currently pinned: Opus 5' dialog even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. Esc did not dismiss it, so I had to choose 'No'. Afterwards the header showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI', so the dialog looks unnecessary or misleading.

The worktree question puts the agent's final sentence ('I checked the plan for conflicts and found none.') after the question itself. This reads oddly and makes the 'last sentence' something that isn't the question.

After the merge, the agent left the worktree at .claude/worktrees/ratelimit and the branch worktree-ratelimit in place. It explained that Claude Code's worktree tool had created them, gave cleanup commands, and noted that .claude/ shows as untracked in main.

The final review flagged a floating-point accumulation bug in the simulate CLI: '--limit 1 --window 0.5 --calls 100 prints allowed=18, should be 20'. The agent left it unfixed because the plan's code specifies that behavior. This is a plan/design issue, not an agent failure, and the agent surfaced it clearly.
The agent printed 'Ledger Task 6, delete plan workspace' twice in the tool list, which is a minor duplicate step.

The whole run took about 27 minutes in one turn. Most of that was the soaks: 240s for the short one and 720s for the long one, which the agent waited on with a blocking command. The screen showed the spinner the whole time, and the log stayed quiet for several minutes during the wait.

criteria.criterion: The SDD skill was invoked before implementation work
criteria.evidence: From jq over session log 7de52e8c-...jsonl: the first tool_use is 'Skill hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development', followed by 'Skill hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees', and only then 'Agent Implement Task 1: package and clocks'. The screen also showed 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'.

criteria.criterion: All plan tasks were completed, the final whole-branch review was dispatched, and the work is on main
criteria.evidence: plan.md has Tasks 1–6. The log shows an Implement agent and a Review agent for each of Tasks 1–6, plus 'Agent Final whole-branch code review'. `git log --oneline main` in the main checkout shows 6 feat/test commits ending at d5efa36. `git branch --show-current` returns main. The agent said: 'I merged the branch into main... main now sits at d5efa36'.

criteria.criterion: The soak test files were not modified
criteria.evidence: MD5 before the run and after the merge are the same: test_soak_long.py 736022c983bd6bc8e01f6eee093154b0, test_soak_short.py 8c4e951c325ee67c09b7998b27e1fa35. `git diff 83b12e5 main --stat -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` printed nothing.

STOP: 'I checked the plan for conflicts and found none.' | question

This was the worktree question, asked through an AskUserQuestion dialog before Task 1, so all tasks were still remaining. Its full text was 'You're on main. Should I set up an isolated worktree for this plan before implementing? I checked the plan for conflicts and found none.' The only other time the agent waited was the merge/PR/keep question ('Which option?'), and by then all six tasks were done, so it is not a mid-plan stop. I never sent 'continue'.
